meaning: The incident and review lessons recorded in the semantic vocabulary RFC's Appendix E, each paired with the probe that retrodicts it against today's guard. A retrodiction asks whether the guard as it exists now rejects the defect form the lesson describes; it does not ask whether a historical revision passed, because the guard did not exist then and that answer is always no. `expectation` is authored from the lesson text, never from probe output; the harness reports where the measurement disagrees with it.

incidents.defect: Parallel constant lists across runtimes pass review until the day one side changes; a parity check must exist before the second copy is accepted.
incidents.expected_rule: A registered cross-runtime vocabulary compares both owner modules against the registry value set.

incidents.defect: A private extraction of a shared constant looks harmless in a large module and is the most common way a schema version forks; test fixtures are second, and HANDOFF_MODES was copied into an e2e fixture.
incidents.expected_rule: A copy outside the scanned roots is either visible to the scan or named as a declared boundary.

incidents.defect: A literal scan that only accepts [a-z_] silently skipped a _v2 spelling; malformed values must be reported, not ignored.
incidents.expected_rule: Quoted literals are captured whatever their shape and the shape is validated separately.

incidents.defect: A scan pattern written from Python examples matched no TypeScript at all, and a guard that is green on a baseline containing violations proves only that it is blind.
incidents.expected_rule: Both runtimes the registry claims to cover are anchored, so dropping one is a failure.

incidents.defect: When the registry is both the specification and the validator's input, a data edit can weaken the validator.
incidents.expected_rule: Recognised forms live in code, coverage counts are floored, and owners must be module::Symbol.

incidents.defect: A ratchet on names alone lets an already-conflicting name gain a third spelling.
incidents.expected_rule: Definition counts and name counts are both budgeted.

incidents.defect: A smoke the fleet discovers is not a commit-time check; if the answer is 'after merge', the invariant is a report, not a gate.
incidents.expected_rule: The guard is selected by the pre-merge planning path for a diff that only touches the guarded code.

incidents.defect: An anchor compared with <= pins only the value it held when written, so every tightening below it is unprotected.
incidents.expected_rule: Budget and floor anchors compare with equality, so neither raising nor lowering the registry value passes.

incidents.defect: One field name can carry several vocabularies inside one envelope; a scan that sees the field cannot see the slot.
incidents.expected_rule: Slots are recorded as a registered relation with an anchored composed domain.

incidents.defect: A committed snapshot of the whole tree makes the guard's input depend on other people's merges.
incidents.expected_rule: The inventory is computed at check time and no snapshot is tracked.

incidents.defect: A name-keyed collision rule needs a way to say 'these are different things that share a name', or the honest fix and a rename lower the same number.
incidents.expected_rule: A declaration names every defining module, so a rename cannot remove the debt.

incidents.defect: When a document widens its scope faster than the code, the two must be reconciled; a scope claim the scanner does not implement is a false invariant.
incidents.expected_rule: The scan's implemented reach is measured at check time and compared with the declared claim.

incidents.defect: Budgets that only go down describe a direction; write the target table before the second milestone, or nobody can say when the work is done.
incidents.expected_rule: The RFC carries a target table whose rows name the surface, the target, and the milestone that reaches it.

incidents.defect: A decision that waits on 'a check' the RFC never defines is a dangling reference dressed as prudence.
incidents.expected_rule: Every open decision names the invariant and the milestone that delivers its input.

incidents.defect: Using a role word nineteen times is not defining it; until the roles are a table with a check per role, 'who writes this value' has no single answer.
incidents.expected_rule: Roles are a declared table with a hierarchy and a producer check that fails closed.

negative_controls.meaning: A closed set with one value is not a twin or a fork, so the collision rule must stay silent.
Two names sharing a generic value set are a review candidate, never an automatic same_concept registration.
The equality anchors accept the registry as committed, so the comparison is not fail-always.
The registry's own owner declarations pass the shape and value checks, so those checks are not fail-always.
The identifier-counting ratchet must not count a longer identifier that merely contains the field name.

caught_baseline.meaning: Frozen at authoring time so the retrodiction cannot silently regress; it records what the guard caught then, not a target.
